snapshot.thesis: How can you not love the Chargers in this matchup? They're much better than the Cardinals. The Chargers are one of the best teams in the NFL, while the Cardinals are in the bottom five. There's a great discrepancy in talent between these teams, and I personally made the spread 14.5. The line is currently only 9.5, which makes no sense to me. If this game were to take place in Week 8, the Chargers would be favored by close to two touchdowns. The only reason this spread is so low is because it's Week 1, and the oddsmakers hate making huge lines during the opening week of the season. This advantage for the Chargers is not even factoring in Jim Harbaugh's pristine Week 1 record. Harbaugh is a perfect 6-0 against the spread in Week 1. Granted, this is a relatively small sample size, but it makes sense that Harbaugh would be dominant to start the year. Harbaugh is a fantastic coach, so if you give someone like him extra time to prepare, he's going to make great use of it. I suspect that this is going to be an ugly blowout. We could see Trey Lance in the fourth quarter.

away: While the Chargers have an exciting new offensive coordinator, they lost their great defensive coordinator, with Jesse Minter taking Baltimore's head-coaching job. Minter had the Chargers as the No. 2 EPA defense last year, so the unit will definitely take a hit. Luckily, the Chargers have a positive matchup to begin the season. Those who enjoyed Arizona's fantasy points last season may disagree that this is a great matchup for the Chargers, but that is truly the case. Arizona did much of its damage last year in garbage time, so its numbers were inflated. For example, when Jacoby Brissett set the single-game record for most completions, he did so when trailing by more than 20 points against the 49ers. The Chargers have a talented pass rush with Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu, as well as first-round rookie Akheem Mesidor. They'll be able to put heat on Brissett throughout the afternoon. The Chargers figure to be worse against the run than the pass this year, but if they're well ahead, as we expect them to be, there won't be many running opportunities for Jeremiyah Love, if he even plays.
home: I'm excited to see what Mike McDaniel can do with the Chargers' offense this year. The Chargers were already expected to bounce back with the health of their tackles, who both missed extensive action last season. Now, McDaniel will be able to take the Chargers out of the Stone Age and bring them into the 21st century. McDaniel should be able to put on a show in this game. He'll have Justin Herbert attack the many weaknesses of Arizona's defense. The Cardinals have some major liabilities at linebacker and cornerback, which Herbert will be able to exploit masterfully. I also expect the Chargers to be able to run the ball easily against the Cardinals. Omarion Hampton projects very well this year, especially with McDaniel. Remember, McDaniel turned journeyman Raheem Mostert into a near-20-touchdown scorer, so imagine what he's going to do with a first-round talent like Hampton.
